verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Nothing is missing and no normative content differs. I rendered page 793 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v793/spec_p793.png) and read it against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. 1) THE HEADINGS ARE PRESENT AND VERBATIM. The PDF page prints exactly two bold headings, '14.9.44.3 Syntax rules' and '14.9.44.4 General rules'. The markdown carries both, with identical text, with the correct dotted section numbers, and with correct anchors ( at line 32140 and at line 32169). Every word of the page's body is also present: Syntax rules ALL FORMATS 1) a)-c), FORMATS 1 AND 2 2)-3), FORMAT 2 4), FORMAT 3 5)-6), and General rules 1) with its (operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n) display. The kind label 'missing-heading' is simply wrong - the only difference is the markdown '#' depth. 2) THE STATED IMPACT IS FALSE FOR THIS REPO'S OWN TOOLING. The claim's whole weight rests on 'any TOC, anchor-walk or section-extraction over the file mis-parents' these blocks. The repository's section extractor, scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, is deliberately heading-level agnostic: HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{2,6}\s+(?P\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+(?P.+?)\s*$") (line 44). It derives hierarchy from the dotted SECTION NUMBER, never from '#' depth, and its own docstring names both depths as normal input ('## 8.4.3.13.3 Syntax rules' at line 12, and line 43-44's 'e.g. "## 8.4.3.13.3 Syntax rules" or "### 14.9.28.4 General rules"'). The authors already knew both shapes occur and treat them identically. So the concrete downstream harm asserted by the claim does not exist. A human or citation-based reader is likewise unaffected: the rendered heading still reads '14.9.44.3', which fixes its parentage unambiguously. 3) THE CAUSE IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE - an explicit reject category. The h2/h3 split is not specific to SUBTRACT; it tracks whether the heading happens to OPEN a printed page, because the transcription was produced one page at a time and a page-opening heading inherits the page block's own h2 level. 14.9.44.3 is the first heading of page 793 (page anchor 32133, '## Page 793' at 32134, heading at 32141). The identical pattern holds elsewhere in the same band: 14.9.40.4 (line 31573) opens page 778, 14.9.48.4 (line 32432) opens page 800, and 14.9.49.3 (line 32597) follows a page-break running header at 32594. 14.9.40.3 (31497) and 14.9.49.4 (32654) are h2 too. So within 14.9.4x itself there are SEVEN four-level headings at h2, not the two the claim isolates - which also undercuts its 'dominant convention' framing as if 14.9.44 were an outlier. 4) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE MARKDOWN'S LOCATIONS. Every cited line number is off by three: 14.9.44.3 is at 32141 (not 32138 - that line is a '---' separator), 14.9.44.4 at 32170 (not 32167 - that is Syntax rule 6), '## 14.9.44 SUBTRACT statement' at 32070 (not 32067), 14.9.44.1 at 32073 and 14.9.44.2 at 32078 (not 32070/32075). Bottom line: no text is missing, no meaning changes, no rule is altered, and the repo's parser is level-agnostic by design. This is a markdown heading-depth inconsistency arising from per-page transcription, i.e. formatting/page-break furniture - not a content discrepancy against the ISO PDF.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a spec-content discrepancy. Both headings are present verbatim with correct section numbers and anchors, and the entire page body matches the PDF. What differs is only the markdown heading DEPTH: 14.9.44.3 and 14.9.44.4 are emitted at h2 rather than h3. This is a repo-wide cosmetic transcription artifact of page-at-a-time extraction (a four-level heading that OPENS a printed page inherits h2), affecting at least 14.9.40.3, 14.9.40.4, 14.9.44.3, 14.9.44.4, 14.9.48.4, 14.9.49.3 and 14.9.49.4. It has no downstream effect, because scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py matches ^#{2,6} and parents sections by their dotted number, not by '#' depth. If anyone wants uniform depth it is a one-line cosmetic sweep over all such page-opening headings, not a page-793 spec-fidelity defect - and it should not be logged in the reconciliation ledger as 'missing-heading', since nothing is missing.
